Technical distillation · completed E01 forensic program

From retrospective PhiID resemblance to a confirmed plastic-heredity risk coordinate

A branch-explicit reconstruction of a recent GARD/PhiID preprint did not support its tested prospective-prediction or causal-control claims. The same program nevertheless identified a different, precisely bounded result: in two reconstructed GARD simulator candidates, present network-conditioned state and recent heredity history predict the independently measured probability that heredity will break and then renew.

Simulator evidence only Two frozen GARD candidates Catalytic matrix = inferential unit Untouched L54 confirmation No causal intervention

Bottom line

Supported

A frozen, target-blind coordinate combining current composition, catalytic-network-conditioned state, growth/fission phase, and recent heredity history ranked a bounded future break-and-renewal probability on new matrices in both simulator candidates.

Not supported

The tested public reconstruction did not establish past-only PhiID prediction of first-replicator appearance, one transferable privileged attractor, Phi-directed causal control, or exact paper-code identity.

Interpretation

The positive result concerns plastic heredity: disruption followed by a new locally hereditary episode, usually without return to the previous molecular composition.

Next scientific gate

Adversarially test target sensitivity, leakage, calibration, preprocessing, candidate robustness, and incremental value over exact H, direct history, ordinary stability, phase, and matrix propensity before any intervention.

Core distinction: the final positive result does not rescue the paper-facing PhiID claim. It replaces both the proposed signal and the proposed event with a prospectively defined simulator-process question.

Questions and evidence architecture

The program began with a forensic question: can the manuscript-visible GARD/Phi-r results be reconstructed from its prose, figures, public GARD history, and PhiRL/IIGR source lineage without inventing missing implementation choices? It then asked a separate scientific question: if the paper-facing pipeline is not identifiable, does reconstructed GARD dynamics contain any reproducible past-observable precursor of future self-maintaining organization?

Compact methods

Reconstruction and numerical controls

The manuscript was decomposed into 59 scientific claims and 120 implementation parameters; unresolved fields remained non-executable rather than being chosen by closeness to the reported results. Historical GARD, PhiRL, IIGR, and PhiID sources were pinned by commit. Domain-separated seeds, exact replay or regeneration, explicit clock and label identities, and CPU-float64 authority were used throughout. Catalytic matrices—not molecular observations or branch futures—were the higher-level independent units.

Paper-facing cohort

The clean S13Y cohort comprised 100 shared catalytic matrices with matched initial states, each run under candidate 02 and candidate 03 for 100 fissions: 200 trajectories. Neither candidate was declared the author implementation. The adjacent molecular label was Yₜ = I(Hₜ > 0.9), with cosine compositional similarity H. Completed-fit PhiRL estimated dimensions, partition, means, and covariance from an entire trajectory and was explicitly marked future-dependent; prefix-only variants used available history only.

Operational process target

Later steps used strict parent-to-selected-daughter H > 0.9 at fission as a local inheritance event, without a completed-run centroid. The final preregistered outcome was:

JOINT_BREAK_RUN3: within the next 12 fissions, heredity breaks and is followed by three consecutive inherited fissions.

An uninterrupted inherited streak did not count as a new episode. The target is bounded, branch-evaluable, and destination-free.

Frozen coordinate and untouched test

L53 adaptively discovered a target-blind representation: 195 molecule-label-permutation-invariant current-state/graph coordinates plus nine direct history/phase variables, development-only scaling, 12-component PCA, and ridge logistic regression with C=0.1. The final F12 transform, PCA, coefficients, probability mapping, landmarks, target, and candidate rules were frozen before L54.

L54 generated 40 new shared matrices, 80 trajectories, and five restored post-fission states per trajectory (400 states). Each state received 64 independent F12 futures split prospectively into two halves of 32: 25,600 branches per campaign, followed by an exact second campaign. Registered analyses included branch-half reliability, calibration, log loss, q-Brier score, overall and matrix-centered Spearman rank, 4,096 matrix bootstraps, and 512 whole-matrix permutations.

Paper-facing reconstruction: resemblance without the claimed inference

The simulator and information pipelines produced abrupt local excursions and some completed-fit association directions resembling the manuscript. Yet the full evidence did not yield one coherent public end-to-end pipeline:

  • Figure 2: positive three-standard-deviation excursions occurred in 90/100 runs per candidate and differenced temporal dependence was widespread, but preregistered aggregate slopes were significantly positive rather than null.
  • Figures 3–4: the closest directions were retrospective, completed-fit, and partly coupled to a stability-derived label.
  • Figure 5: adjacent-H targets were nearly always positive, so raw accuracy was shared by learned models and the majority dummy. Recurring-target and padding/length audits did not produce a valid prospective reconstruction.
  • Figure 6/Table 1: a literal online scorer was executable and replayable, but max/control/min ordering and causal control were not recovered.

The supported items were mainly technical or broad directional properties. Prospective prediction and bidirectional causal control did not pass. Missing author code means this is a verdict on the tested public reconstruction, not proof that a private implementation cannot produce the manuscript's results.

Why the target changed: committor signal, nontransferable destination

Restoring simulator states and launching independent future ensembles established that a completed-run attractor-entry target had a reliable state-dependent finite-horizon probability. Independent 64-branch halves gave split-half Spearman correlations of 0.926 and 0.933, and a short eight-observation propagator later ranked that probability on untouched matrices.

However, separate lineages under the same catalytic matrix did not reliably select one reciprocal basin or basin family. A completed-run target could therefore be predictable while remaining trajectory-specific. This invalidated its interpretation as a general “replicator destination” and motivated a process outcome recognizable without the evaluated lineage's future.

Plastic heredity: disruption and renewal without compositional restoration

Parent–daughter inheritance was common but not uninterrupted. Across registered L44 validation and confirmation cohorts:

  • inheritance-break probability was approximately 0.64–0.73;
  • three-fission inherited-episode probability was approximately 0.76–0.82;
  • five-fission episode probability was approximately 0.53–0.60;
  • resumption given a break was approximately 0.88–0.91;
  • old-neighbourhood event prevalence was only approximately 0.0026–0.0069, with a separate conditional-on-break recovery estimate of approximately 0.0024–0.0051;
  • mean similarity gain toward the old anchor at resumption was about −0.26.

Count-matched order permutations and small Markov-over-IID information gains indicated sticky local episodes, but did not establish biological memory, functional restoration, or error correction. Past-only PhiID added no held-out value beyond direct heredity controls.

Untouched confirmation of a past-observable process-risk coordinate

The empirical F12 process probability was neither constant nor dominated by branch noise: 138/200 and 149/200 states lay in the intermediate region 0.1 < q < 0.9. Independent branch halves were strongly reliable, including after matrix-centering.

Bounded conclusion: reconstructed GARD contains a past-observable propensity for a specific plastic-heredity regime transition. The result predicts an independently estimated stochastic probability—not the deterministic future of an individual trajectory.

Interpretation and claim boundary

The evidence supportsThe evidence does not support
A validated family of explicit reconstructed simulator branchesIdentity with the unavailable author implementation
Partial retrospective resemblance to paper-visible Phi dynamicsPast-only PhiID warning of first self-replicator appearance
A reliable committor for a completed-run targetOne stable cross-lineage privileged attractor
Plastic renewal of local hereditary episodes under the registered definitionsFixed-composition restoration, homeostasis, or independent functional memory
Untouched probability ranking and proper-score improvement by a frozen state/graph/history coordinateIntervention efficacy, causal control, biological heredity, or prebiotic validation

The result is consistent with a network–state–history interaction: catalytic network × current composition/state × recent hereditary history and phase. It is not yet a compact physical law. The 195-coordinate graph/state representation and PCA are engineered, calibration is imperfect, confirmation spans 40 matrices and five landmarks, and discovery before L54 was highly adaptive.

Novelty boundary. Prior work already establishes GARD compositional heredity, compotypes, catalytic-network effects, PhiID, causal emergence, and committor learning. The potentially novel element is their operational combination here: a destination-free break-plus-renewal event, empirical branch probability, target-blind network/state/history representation, and untouched transfer in two reconstructed candidates. A literature search found no direct match, but absence of a match is not proof of priority.

Falsification priorities

  1. Adversarial E02 validation: freeze and test future-suffix leakage, target/preprocessing sensitivity, numerical robustness, candidate consistency, and calibration.
  2. Stronger controls: require incremental value beyond exact H, direct history, ordinary stability, phase, matrix propensity, and simpler state/process coordinates.
  3. Mechanistic compression: test preregistered grouped ablations and interpretable students without tuning on confirmation outcomes.
  4. Broader scope: evaluate new matrix distributions, simulator regimes, phases, and process targets.
  5. Only after survival: use matched stochastic futures to test whether small molecular edits that move the frozen score also move the independently estimated F12 probability.

Until those gates pass, the coordinate should be treated as a nonprivileged candidate replacement architecture variable. PhiID remains a nonprivileged comparator, and intervention claims remain inactive.
